recognize_zh: 周邊血液中一顆約為紅血球1.5–2倍大的圓形細胞，核質比極高，只見一圈薄薄的藍色細胞質，核染色質均勻細點狀、核仁不明顯，沒有顆粒，符合淋巴母細胞（lymphoblast）。
features: Single round cell roughly 1.5-2 times the diameter of a red cell
Very high N:C ratio with only a thin rim of basophilic cytoplasm
Round nucleus with homogeneous, finely stippled chromatin that is more condensed than a myeloblast
Background normocytic red cells and small platelet clumps
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single circulating blast approximately one and a half to two times the size of a red cell. The cell has a very high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio with a thin rim of agranular basophilic cytoplasm, a round nucleus, and homogeneous finely stippled chromatin with inconspicuous nucleoli. No Auer rods are present. Red cells appear normocytic, and small platelet clumps are seen. Morphology is suggestive of a lymphoblast; confirmation requires flow cytometric immunophenotyping.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts are usually larger with more cytoplasm, very fine open chromatin, distinct nucleoli, and may show granules or Auer rods, whereas this cell has scant cytoplasm and more condensed chromatin.
Mature lymphocytes are smaller with dense, coarsely clumped chromatin and no nucleoli rather than the fine, even chromatin of a blast.
Hematogones have very homogeneous smudged chromatin and scant cytoplasm and can be indistinguishable morphologically, requiring flow cytometry to show normal maturation patterns.
